front: Why is shuffled KFold wrong for time series?
back: Neighbouring days are similar and future rows enter training. The score is too optimistic compared with the real forecast.
Leaves g rows between the end of training and the start of the test block, to avoid overlap leakage.
y.shift(1).rolling(7).mean(): the window ends one step before the row.

front: Why use a Pipeline in cross-validation?
back: Scalers and imputers are fitted only on each training fold, so test statistics do not leak.
The automatic validation split is random, not time-ordered. Use early_stopping=False or your own time-based validation.

front: Why can trees fail on trending data?
back: They output averages of training targets, so they cannot go beyond seen values. Predict the difference instead.
